The team's head coach was [[Bruce Pearl]] in his 11th and final season at Auburn. The team played its home games at [[Neville Arena]] in [[Auburn, Alabama]]. Pearl won his 214th game for Auburn at [[2024–25 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]] on January 7, surpassing [[Joel Eaves]] for the most wins in school history.{{Cite web |date=2025-01-08 |title=Auburn head basketball coach Bruce Pearl offers emotional thoughts on making history with win over Texas {{!}} Sporting News |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/auburn-head-basketball-coach-bruce-pearl-offers-emotional-thoughts-making-history-win-over-texas/4e226e52a87e4caa0d9ede70 |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=www.sportingnews.com |language=en-us}} Auburn finished the season with a {{Win-loss record|w=32|l=6}} overall record and a {{Win-loss record|w=15|l=3}} mark in SEC play, earning the program the No. 1 overall seed in the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2025 NCAA tournament]]. As the No. 1 seed in the [[2025 SEC men's basketball tournament|2025 SEC Tournament]], held at [[Bridgestone Arena]] in [[Nashville, Tennessee]], Auburn began its postseason run in the quarterfinals with a 62–57 victory over No. 8 seed [[2024–25 Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball team|Ole Miss]]. In the semifinals, the Tigers faced No. 4 seed [[2024–25 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] and were narrowly defeated 70–65, ending their bid for the conference tournament title. Auburn received a bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2025 NCAA tournament]], as the tournament's No. 1 overall seed. They were seeded in the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#South regional – Atlanta, Georgia|South region]]. In the First Round, the Tigers defeated No. 16 seed [[2024–25 Alabama State Hornets basketball team|Alabama State]], 83–63. They went on to beat No. 9 seed [[2024–25 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]], 82–70, in the Second Round. In the Sweet Sixteen, Auburn overcame No. 5 seed [[2024–25 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] with a 78–65 victory. In the Elite Eight, they defeated No. 2 seed [[2024–25 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] by a score of 70–64 to claim the South Regional title and advance to the Final Four for the second time in school history. However, their season came to an end with a 79–73 loss to SEC rival and [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|eventual champion]] [[2024–25 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] in the Final Four. [[Chad Baker-Mazara]] led Auburn with 18 points, while [[Johni Broome]] added 15 points and seven rebounds despite playing through a right elbow injury that limited his second-half performance. Auburn's 32 victories in the 2024–25 season surpassed the program's previous single-season record set by the [[2018-19 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|2018–19 team]], which won 30 games. Pearl would retire from coaching only a month prior to the [[2025–26 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|2025–26 season]], leaving his son [[Steven Pearl|Steven]] in charge. ==Previous season== The [[2023–24 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team]] finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] with a record of 27–8, 13–5 in [[Southeastern Conference]] play to finish tied for second place in the conference. As the No. 4 seed in the [[2024 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], they defeated [[2023–24 South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball team|South Carolina]], [[2023–24 Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball team|Mississippi State]], and [[2023–24 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] to win the tournament championship. The Tigers received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 4 seed in the East Region.
